newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall 2.05 percent on bank sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall 2.05 percent on bank sales.

text.p: Thai stocks fell 2.05 percent by 0849 GMT as profit taking in key blue chips, after two days of strong gains, spilled over to banking stocks, traders said.

The SET Index fell 10.36 points to 494.17 midway through the afternoon session after briefly hitting a day-low of 493.82. The SET 50 fell 0.80 points, or 2.24 percent to 35.08 in trade worth 3.67 billion baht.

After around an eight percent gain in the market over the last two trading days, the temptation to take profits ahead of a parliamentary budget debate on Wednesday and economic data released on Thursday proved irresistable, traders said.
"Today it has just proved to be unsustainable on the fundamentals since the fundamentals haven't changed. I think yesterday's rally was very technical," said a trader at Thai Farmers Bank affiliate.
Profit taking spilled over to bank stocks and gains in communications shares, which had supported the market against heavy sales of finance counters, saw earlier premiums fall.
Bangkok Bank Plc fell four baht to 115 by 0857 GMT. Thai Farmers shed three to 79 and Thai Military Bank was down two to 25.25.
